text.p: Lithuanian newspapers carried the following reports in their Monday editions. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy:
- American Senator Richard Durbin, a staunch supporter of Baltic interests, arrived in Vilnius on Saturday. Durbin said that he has no doubts that Lithuania will join NATO.
- The crime-ridden city of Panevezys was the scene of another vigilante shooting inncident. Businessman Algimantas Kisielis shot two masked robbers who attacked him Friday night, one of them fatally.
- The privatisation deals of Lithuanian Savings bank in 1993 were sectret and illegal.
- Twenty-four political parties and organisations intend to participate in the municipal elections in March.

- Analysts say that the ban on tobacco and alcohol will bankrupt Lithuanian basketball. Philip Morris Lietuva, alcohol importer Bennet Distributors and brewery Kalnapilis had committed 300,000 litas to sponsor the country's national basketball leauge this year.

- Communications minister Rimantas Pleikys says that disorganization in Lithuanian Telecom could be changed only by the privatisation of the company. The Lithuanian government has decided to privatise Telecom and the minister thinks that privatisation in reality might start in 1998- 1999.

- Estonian Hoiupank intends to use its priority right and acquire shares in the new emission of Hermis bank. Hermis bank decided last week to boost its share capital to 90 million litas from 67 million litas.

- Lithuanian President Algirdas Brazauskas on Saturday appealed for an end to partisan conflict and asked all political parties to sign an act of concord "to solve together the growing problems in the country".
- The Statistics department says that there are 370 people from 32 countries studying in Lithuania's universities.
- The chairman of the board of Siauliu bank Zenonas Sabalys forecasts in an interview that profit in 1996 will br four million litas.
